entries.desc: Muhammad Ahmad's Mahdist Sudanese forces overthrew Ottoman-Egyptian rule and later fought the British, establishing an independent Mahdist state in Sudan.

entries.name: Battle of Almansa
entries.desc: Decisive Bourbon victory over Habsburg forces during the War of the Spanish Succession, securing Philip V's hold on Spain.

entries.name: Battle of Solferino
entries.desc: Franco-Piedmontese victory over Austria that was the climactic battle of the Second Italian War of Independence.

entries.name: Siege of Acre
entries.desc: Mamluk capture of the last Crusader stronghold in the Holy Land, ending nearly two centuries of Crusader presence in the Levant.

entries.name: Battle of Marston Moor
entries.desc: Parliamentarian and Scottish Covenanter victory over Royalist forces, the largest battle of the Wars of the Three Kingdoms.

entries.name: Nakba
entries.desc: Mass displacement and dispossession of Palestinian Arabs accompanying the establishment of Israel in 1948.

entries.name: Battle of Morgarten
entries.desc: Swiss Confederate ambush that destroyed an invading Austrian army, a founding victory of the Old Swiss Confederacy.

entries.name: Battle of Gazala
entries.desc: Axis victory over British Commonwealth forces in the Western Desert Campaign that led to the fall of Tobruk.

entries.name: Operation Nordwind
entries.desc: Last major German offensive on the Western Front, launched to relieve pressure from the Battle of the Bulge.

entries.name: Battle of Aachen
entries.desc: Bitter urban battle in which American forces captured the first major German city of World War II.

entries.name: Battle of Białystok–Minsk
entries.desc: German encirclement that destroyed two Soviet armies in the opening days of Operation Barbarossa.

entries.name: Battle of Uman
entries.desc: German offensive that encircled and annihilated two Soviet armies near Uman, Ukraine, in 1941.

entries.name: Machtergreifung
entries.desc: Adolf Hitler's rise to the German chancellorship and the Nazi Party's subsequent consolidation of dictatorial power.

entries.name: Battle of Varna
entries.desc: Ottoman victory over a Crusader army led by Władysław III of Poland and Hungary, ending the Crusade of Varna.

entries.name: First Boer War
entries.desc: Boer victory over British forces in the Transvaal that restored South African Republic independence.

entries.name: War of the Austrian Succession
entries.desc: Multi-power European conflict sparked by Maria Theresa's succession to the Habsburg throne.

entries.name: Battle of Marignano
entries.desc: French and Venetian victory over the Old Swiss Confederacy that ended the War of the League of Cambrai.

entries.name: Battle of Gettysburg
entries.desc: Union victory over Confederate forces widely regarded as the turning point of the American Civil War.

entries.name: Battle of Eylau
entries.desc: Bloody, inconclusive clash between Napoleon's Grande Armée and Russian forces in East Prussia.

entries.name: Seven Years' War
entries.desc: Global conflict pitting Britain and Prussia against France, Austria, and their allies across Europe, the Americas, and India.

entries.name: Battle of the Pyramids
entries.desc: Napoleon's victory over Ottoman Egyptian forces near Cairo during the French invasion of Egypt.

entries.name: Battle of Bunker Hill
entries.desc: On 17 June 1775, British troops took the Charlestown peninsula near Boston from American militia in a costly frontal assault. Britain's heavy casualties in the technical victory showed the war would not be quickly won.

entries.name: Battle of Monte Cassino
entries.desc: Fought across four Allied assaults between January and May 1944, this battle broke the German Gustav Line defenses south of Rome, at the cost of the historic abbey's destruction, and opened the road to Rome.

entries.name: Battle of Grunwald
entries.desc: On 15 July 1410, a Polish–Lithuanian–Ruthenian army decisively defeated the Teutonic Knights near Grunwald, killing the order's Grand Master. The defeat broke the Teutonic Order's military dominance in the region.

entries.name: Battle of Großbeeren
entries.desc: On 23 August 1813, Prussian forces under Friedrich von Bülow defeated a Franco-Saxon corps south of Berlin. The victory blocked a French advance on the city during the War of the Sixth Coalition.

entries.name: Battle of the Milvian Bridge
entries.desc: The Battle of the Milvian Bridge took place between the Roman Emperors Constantine I and Maxentius on 28 October AD 312. It takes its name from the Milvian Bridge, an important route over the Tiber.

entries.name: transition from Ming to Qing
entries.desc: The transition from Ming to Qing, also known as the Manchu conquest of China or Ming–Qing transition, was a decades-long period of conflict between the Qing dynasty, established by the Manchu Aisin…

entries.name: Battle of Okehazama
entries.desc: On 12 June 1560, Oda Nobunaga's greatly outnumbered forces ambushed and killed rival warlord Imagawa Yoshimoto, an upset victory that launched Nobunaga's rise toward unifying Japan.

entries.name: Adams–Onís Treaty
entries.desc: Signed in 1819 by John Quincy Adams and Luis de Onís, this treaty ceded Spanish Florida to the United States and fixed the western border between the US and New Spain along a line to the Pacific.

entries.desc: The Partitio terrarum imperii Romaniae, or Partitio regni Graeci, was a treaty signed among the crusaders after the sack of the Byzantine capital, Constantinople, by the Fourth Crusade in 1204. It …

entries.name: Arab conquest of Armenia
entries.desc: A series of Rashidun Caliphate campaigns from 639 to 661 against Byzantine-held Armenia. The fighting brought Armenia under Arab suzerainty while its local nakharar princes retained considerable autonomy.

entries.name: Anglo-Spanish War
entries.desc: A conflict from 1654 to 1660 in which Oliver Cromwell's England attacked Spain's American and European possessions as part of the "Western Design." England seized Jamaica from Spain during the fighting.

entries.desc: The Siege of Baghdad, also known as the Sack of Baghdad, took place in early 1258. A large army commanded by Hulegu, a prince of the Mongol Empire, attacked the historic capital of the Abbasid Cali…

entries.name: Battle of Tippecanoe
entries.desc: On 7 November 1811, American forces under William Henry Harrison defeated Tecumseh's Native confederacy while Tecumseh was away, dispersing the alliance and giving Harrison a reputation he later rode to the presidency.

entries.name: Caucasian War
entries.desc: A prolonged conflict in which the Russian Empire subdued the peoples of the North Caucasus who resisted subjugation during the Russian conquest of the region, ending in annexation and the mass expulsion of Circassians.

entries.name: Battle of Saragarhi
entries.desc: On 12 September 1897, 21 soldiers of the 36th Sikhs held a signalling post against thousands of Afghan tribesmen, fighting to the last man; the stand is remembered as one of history's celebrated last stands.

entries.name: Battle of Kohima
entries.desc: Fought from April to June 1944, this battle halted Japan's invasion of British India; combined with the victory at Imphal, it forced a costly Japanese retreat and marked the turning point of the Burma campaign.

entries.name: Battle of Mukden
entries.desc: Fought from February to March 1905, this was the largest land battle fought before World War I; Japan's victory over the Russian army effectively ended Russian land resistance in the Russo-Japanese War.

entries.name: Battle of the Yalu River
entries.desc: On 17 September 1894, Japan's navy decisively defeated China's Beiyang Fleet at the mouth of the Yalu River, establishing Japanese naval supremacy for the remainder of the First Sino-Japanese War.

entries.name: Battle of Dara
entries.desc: The Battle of Dara was fought between the Eastern Roman Empire and the Sasanians in 530 AD. It was one of the battles of the Iberian War.

entries.name: Ōnin War
entries.desc: The Ōnin War , also known as the Upheaval of Ōnin and Ōnin-Bunmei war, was a civil war that lasted from 1467 to 1477, during the Muromachi period in Japan. Ōnin refers to the Japanese era during wh…

entries.name: Treaty of Hadiach
entries.desc: The Treaty of Hadiach was a treaty signed on 16 September 1658 in Hadiach, Cossack Hetmanate between representatives of the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth and Zaporozhian Cossacks.

entries.name: Battle of Arnhem
entries.desc: The Battle of Arnhem was fought during the Second World War, as part of the Allied Operation Market Garden. It took place around the Dutch city of Arnhem from 17 to 26 September 1944.

entries.name: Battle of Stalingrad
entries.desc: Fought from August 1942 to February 1943, Soviet forces encircled and destroyed Germany's Sixth Army in the deadliest battle in history, marking the turning point of World War II on the Eastern Front.

entries.name: Battle of Yamazaki

entries.name: Battle of Soissons
entries.desc: In 486, Frankish king Clovis I defeated the Roman general Syagrius near Soissons, ending the last vestige of Roman rule in northern Gaul and opening the region to Frankish control.

entries.name: Battle of Sagrajas
entries.desc: In 1086, Almoravid forces under Yusuf ibn Tashfin defeated Alfonso VI of Castile at Sagrajas, checking the Christian reconquest of Iberia and opening al-Andalus to decades of Almoravid rule.

entries.name: Battle of Vimy Ridge
entries.desc: In April 1917, the four divisions of the Canadian Corps captured German-held Vimy Ridge in a costly, coordinated assault that is remembered in Canada as a defining moment of national identity.

entries.name: Battle of Coronel
entries.desc: On 1 November 1914, a German East Asia Squadron under Maximilian von Spee defeated a British squadron under Christopher Cradock off Chile, sinking two cruisers. It was the Royal Navy's first defeat at sea in a century.

entries.name: Battle of Dettingen
entries.desc: Fought on 27 June 1743 near Dettingen in Bavaria during the War of the Austrian Succession, an allied army defeated the French. It was the last time a reigning British monarch personally led troops into battle.

entries.name: Battle of Pliska
entries.desc: In July 811, Bulgarian forces under Khan Krum ambushed and destroyed the Byzantine army in the Balkan passes, killing Emperor Nicephorus I, whose skull Krum reportedly had made into a drinking cup.

entries.name: Attack of the Dead Men
entries.desc: The Attack of the Dead Men, or the Battle of Osowiec Fortress, was a battle of World War I that took place at Osowiec Fortress, at 4:00 AM on August 6, 1915.

entries.name: Battle of Denain
entries.desc: On 24 July 1712, French forces under Marshal Villars defeated a Dutch and Austrian army near Denain during the War of the Spanish Succession, reversing France's decline and easing peace terms at Utrecht.

entries.name: Second Opium War
entries.desc: The Second Opium War, also known as the Second Anglo-Chinese War or Arrow War, was fought between the United Kingdom and France against the Qing dynasty of China between 1856 and 1860. It was the s…

entries.name: Battle of New Orleans
entries.desc: On 8 January 1815, Andrew Jackson's American forces decisively defeated the British army outside New Orleans, fought after the war-ending Treaty of Ghent had already been signed, and made Jackson a national hero.

entries.name: Philippine Revolution
entries.desc: The Philippine Revolution was a war of independence waged by the revolutionary organization Katipunan against the Spanish Empire from 1896 to 1898. It was the culmination of the 333-year colonial r…

entries.name: Gunboat War
entries.desc: Naval conflict between Denmark–Norway and Britain, supported by Sweden, during the Napoleonic Wars.

entries.name: Third Battle of Ypres
entries.desc: Also known as Passchendaele, a WWI campaign fought by the Allies against Germany near Ypres, Belgium.

entries.name: Battle of Nagashino
entries.desc: Allied forces of Oda Nobunaga and Tokugawa Ieyasu decisively defeated the Takeda clan.

entries.name: Great Sioux War of 1876
entries.desc: War between the US and allied Lakota Sioux and Northern Cheyenne forces over the Black Hills.

entries.name: Arauco War
entries.desc: Long conflict between Spanish colonizers and the Mapuche people in Chile's Araucanía region.

entries.name: Battle of White Mountain
entries.desc: Early Thirty Years' War battle near Prague where forces backing Ferdinand II defeated Frederick V's army.

entries.name: Battle of Valmy
entries.desc: France's first major Revolutionary War victory, halting a Prussian advance on Paris.

entries.name: Battle of the Golden Spurs
entries.desc: Flemish rebels won a surprise victory over the French royal army near Kortrijk in 1302.

entries.name: Siege of Yorktown
entries.desc: Final major land battle of the American Revolutionary War, won by American and French forces.

entries.name: Franco-Prussian War
entries.desc: Conflict between France and the Prussian-led North German Confederation, 1870–71.

entries.name: Svalbard Treaty
entries.desc: Recognized Norwegian sovereignty over the Svalbard archipelago while restricting its military use.

entries.name: November Uprising
entries.desc: Armed rebellion by Polish officers in Warsaw against Russian imperial rule, 1830–31.

entries.name: Entente Cordiale
entries.desc: Agreements signed in 1904 that markedly improved relations between the UK and France.

entries.name: Battle of Balaclava
entries.desc: Crimean War battle near Sevastopol between British, French, and Ottoman allies and Russian forces.

entries.name: Battle of Wagram
entries.desc: Napoleon's costly but decisive victory over Austria that broke up the Fifth Coalition.

entries.name: First Barbary War
entries.desc: The US fought Ottoman Tripolitania over tribute demands for safe passage of American shipping.

entries.name: Battle of Suomussalmi
entries.desc: Finnish forces defeated a much larger Soviet army during the Winter War of 1939–40.

entries.name: Battle of Kulm
entries.desc: The Battle of Kulm was fought near the town Kulm and the village Přestanov in northern Bohemia. It was fought on 29–30 August 1813, during the War of the Sixth Coalition.

entries.name: Battle of Waterloo
entries.desc: On 18 June 1815, Anglo-allied forces under Wellington and Prussian forces under Blücher defeated Napoleon near Waterloo, ending his rule permanently and bringing the Napoleonic Wars to a close.

entries.name: Battle of Badr
entries.desc: Fought on 13 March 624 CE near Badr in the Hejaz, this battle saw a small Muslim force under Muhammad defeat a larger Meccan army. The unexpected victory established Muhammad's authority and is commemorated in the Quran.

entries.name: Battle of Uhud
entries.desc: The Battle of Uhud was fought between the early Muslims and the Quraysh during the Muslim–Quraysh wars in a valley north of Medina near Mount Uhud on Saturday, 23 March 625 AD.

entries.name: 1948 Arab–Israeli War
entries.desc: The interstate phase of the 1948 Palestine war, fought between Israel and neighboring Arab states after Israel declared independence. Israel won, gaining more land than the UN partition plan had proposed.

entries.name: 1948 Palestine war
entries.desc: Civil war between Palestine's Arab and Jewish communities after the UN partition vote, ending with British withdrawal and Israeli independence. It caused Palestinian displacement and led into the wider Arab–Israeli war.

entries.name: Battle of Talas
entries.desc: In July 751, Abbasid and allied forces defeated Tang China's army near the Talas River, halting Chinese expansion into Central Asia and, by tradition, helping papermaking technology spread to the Islamic world.

entries.name: Battle of Cold Harbor
entries.desc: Fought near Mechanicsville, Virginia, from 31 May to 12 June 1864, Union assaults on entrenched Confederate lines were repulsed with heavy losses. It is remembered as one of Grant's costliest failures of the war.

entries.name: Battle of Stirling Bridge
entries.desc: On 11 September 1297, Scottish forces under William Wallace and Andrew Moray defeated a larger English army by exploiting a narrow river crossing, a decisive early victory in the Wars of Scottish Independence.

entries.name: Battle of Guadalete
entries.desc: Fought in July 711 in southern Spain, Umayyad forces under Tariq ibn Ziyad defeated the Visigothic army of King Roderic, who was killed. The victory opened the way for the swift Muslim conquest of the Iberian Peninsula.

entries.name: Battle of Dobro Pole
entries.desc: An Allied offensive on the Macedonian front from 15 to 18 September 1918 broke through Bulgarian lines at Dobro Pole. The breakthrough led directly to Bulgaria's surrender that month, the first Central Power to fall.

entries.name: Battle of the Korsun–Cherkassy Pocket
entries.desc: Fought from January to February 1944, Soviet forces encircled two German army corps near Korsun, destroying much of the trapped force and marking a major Red Army victory of the Dnieper–Carpathian offensive.

entries.name: Battle of Cherbourg
entries.desc: The Battle of Cherbourg was part of the Battle of Normandy during World War II. It was fought immediately after the successful Allied landings on 6 June 1944.

entries.name: People's Crusade
entries.desc: The People's Crusade was the beginning phase of the First Crusade whose objective was to retake the Holy Land, and Jerusalem in particular, from Islamic rule. In 1095, after the head of the Catholi…

entries.name: Battle of Zenta
entries.desc: On 11 September 1697, Habsburg forces under Prince Eugene of Savoy destroyed an Ottoman army crossing the Tisza River, a victory that led to the Treaty of Karlowitz and ended Ottoman expansion into Central Europe.

entries.name: King George's War
entries.desc: King George's War (1744–1748) encompassed the military operations in North America that formed part of the War of the Austrian Succession (1740–1748). It was the third of the four French and Indian…

entries.name: Battle of the Neva
entries.desc: In 1240, Novgorod forces under Prince Alexander defeated an invading Swedish force on the Neva River, a victory that earned him the epithet 'Nevsky' and became a lasting symbol of Russian resistance to Western incursion.

entries.name: Attack on Pearl Harbor
entries.desc: Japan launched a surprise strike on the US Pacific Fleet at Pearl Harbor, Hawaii, on 7 December 1941, sinking or damaging much of the battle fleet. The attack brought the United States into the Second World War.

entries.name: Cologne War
entries.desc: From 1583 to 1588, Catholic forces led by Bavaria's Duke Ernest defeated Protestant claimant Gebhard Truchsess von Waldburg for control of the Electorate of Cologne, reasserting Catholic rule in the region.

entries.desc: The Persian expedition of Catherine the Great of 1796, like the Persian expedition of Peter the Great (1722–1723), was one of the Russo-Persian Wars of the 18th century which did not entail any las…

entries.name: Treaty of Pereyaslav
entries.desc: The Pereiaslav Agreement or Pereyaslav Agreement was an official meeting that convened for a ceremonial pledge of allegiance by Zaporozhian Cossacks to Russian tsar Alexis in the town of Pereiaslav…

entries.name: Treaty of Georgievsk
entries.desc: The Treaty of Georgievsk was a bilateral treaty concluded between the Russian Empire and the east Georgian kingdom of Kartli-Kakheti on July 24, 1783. The treaty established eastern Georgia as a pr…

entries.name: Battle of Westerplatte
entries.desc: On 1 September 1939, German forces attacked the small Polish garrison at Westerplatte, the opening engagement of the invasion of Poland and the start of World War II in Europe.

entries.name: Treaty of Saadabad
entries.desc: The Treaty of Saadabad was a non-aggression pact signed by Turkey, Iran, Iraq and Afghanistan on 8 July 1937, and lasted for five years. The treaty was signed in Tehran's Saadabad Palace and was pa…

entries.name: Anglo-Japanese Alliance
entries.desc: A mutual-defense pact between Britain and Japan signed in 1902, aimed chiefly at containing Russian expansion in East Asia. It underpinned Japan's rise as a great power until it lapsed in 1923.

entries.name: Battle of Prokhorovka
entries.desc: Fought on 12 July 1943 as part of the Battle of Kursk, this was one of the largest tank engagements of World War II; it checked the German southern advance and helped end Germany's last major offensive in the East.

entries.name: Battle of Aspern-Essling
entries.desc: In May 1809, Austrian forces under Archduke Charles drove Napoleon's army back across the Danube near Vienna. It was Napoleon's first major defeat in the field, though he recovered and won at Wagram weeks later.

entries.name: Battle of Alam el Halfa
entries.desc: In late August and early September 1942, Britain's Eighth Army under Montgomery repelled Rommel's attempt to break through south of El Alamein. The failed offensive left the Axis unable to threaten Egypt again.

entries.name: Battle of Fort Sumter
entries.desc: Confederate forces bombarded the Union-held Fort Sumter in Charleston Harbor on 12–13 April 1861, forcing its surrender without loss of life on either side, in the opening engagement of the American Civil War.

entries.name: Battle of Taranto
entries.desc: On the night of 11–12 November 1940, British carrier aircraft crippled the Italian fleet at anchor at Taranto in the first all-aircraft ship-to-ship attack in naval history, later studied by planners of Pearl Harbor.

entries.name: War of Jenkins' Ear
entries.desc: The War of Jenkins' Ear was fought between Great Britain and Spain from 1739 to 1748. Most of the fighting took place in New Granada and the Caribbean Sea, with major operations over by 1742.

entries.name: Treaty of Versailles (1871)
entries.desc: The Treaty of Versailles of 1871 ended the Franco-Prussian War and was signed by Adolphe Thiers of the Third French Republic and Otto von Bismarck of the newly formed German Empire on 26 February 1…

entries.name: Battle of Maiwand
entries.desc: On 27 July 1880, Afghan forces under Ayub Khan defeated a British-Indian brigade near Kandahar, one of Britain's costliest defeats of the Second Anglo-Afghan War, though British troops recaptured Kandahar weeks later.

entries.name: War of the Breton Succession
entries.desc: The War of the Breton Succession or Breton Civil War was a conflict between the Counts of Blois and the Montforts of Brittany for control of the Duchy of Brittany. It was fought between 1341 and 12…

entries.name: Battle of Azaz
entries.desc: In 1125, a Crusader army under Baldwin II of Jerusalem defeated a Seljuk and Artuqid coalition near Azaz, relieving pressure on Antioch and Aleppo and checking Muslim efforts to reunite northern Syria.

entries.name: Battle of Berezina
entries.desc: Between 26 and 29 November 1812, Napoleon's retreating army forced a crossing of the Berezina River under Russian attack. It survived encirclement but suffered catastrophic losses in the disaster of the Russian campaign.

entries.name: First Silesian War
entries.desc: The First Silesian War was a war between Prussia and Austria that lasted from 1740 to 1742 and resulted in Prussia's seizure of most of the region of Silesia from Austria. The war was fought mainly…

entries.name: Defense of the Polish Post Office in Danzig
entries.desc: On 1 September 1939, Polish postal workers defended their post office in Danzig against German attack on the invasion's first day; most surviving defenders were later executed by German forces.

entries.name: Battle of Khaybar
entries.desc: In 628 CE, Muhammad's forces besieged the Jewish community at the Khaybar oasis, who surrendered and were allowed to keep farming the land in exchange for tribute, until their later expulsion under Caliph Umar.

entries.name: League of the Three Emperors
entries.desc: The League of the Three Emperors or Union of the Three Emperors was an alliance between the German, Russian and Austro-Hungarian Empires, from 1873 to 1887. Chancellor Otto von Bismarck took full c…

entries.name: Battle of Fontenoy
entries.desc: On 11 May 1745, a French army under Marshal Saxe defeated an allied British, Dutch, and Hanoverian force near Fontenoy during the War of the Austrian Succession, opening France's conquest of the Austrian Netherlands.

entries.name: Battle of the Kalka River
entries.desc: In 1223, Mongol forces under Jebe and Subutai defeated a coalition of Rus' princes at the Kalka River, a shock defeat that previewed the full Mongol invasion of Rus' lands over a decade later.

entries.name: Battle of Rossbach
entries.desc: On 5 November 1757, Frederick the Great's outnumbered Prussian army routed a combined French and Imperial force during the Seven Years' War, a lopsided defeat that later spurred French military reforms.

entries.name: Fourth Anglo-Dutch War
entries.desc: The Fourth Anglo-Dutch War was a conflict between the Kingdom of Great Britain and the Dutch Republic. The war, contemporary with the American Revolutionary War (1775–1783), broke out over British …

entries.name: Battle of Cresson
entries.desc: On 1 May 1187, a small force of Templars and Hospitallers was destroyed by an Ayyubid raiding party under Saladin near the Spring of Cresson. It foreshadowed the far larger Crusader disaster at Hattin two months later.

entries.name: Battle of Forbie
entries.desc: On 17–18 October 1244, an Ayyubid and Khwarazmian army crushed a combined Crusader and Ayyubid force near Forbie, killing or capturing most of the Crusader army, which could no longer mount another major offensive.

entries.name: Battle of Blore Heath
entries.desc: Fought on 23 September 1459 in Staffordshire, this early battle of the Wars of the Roses saw a Yorkist force under the Earl of Salisbury defeat a larger Lancastrian army sent to intercept it.

entries.name: First Anglo-Sikh War
entries.desc: The First Anglo-Sikh War was fought between the Sikh Empire and the British Empire from 1845 to 1846 around the Firozpur district of Punjab. It resulted in the defeat and partial subjugation of the…

entries.name: Battle of Debrecen
entries.desc: The Battle of Debrecen, called by the Red Army the Debrecen Offensive Operation, was a battle taking place from 6 to 29 October 1944 on the Eastern Front in Hungary during World War II.

entries.name: Battle of Kleidion
entries.desc: On 29 July 1014, Byzantine emperor Basil II crushed the Bulgarian army and blinded thousands of captives, breaking Bulgarian resistance and paving the way for Byzantium to annex Bulgaria by 1018.

entries.name: Battle of Falkirk
entries.desc: On 22 July 1298, an English army under Edward I defeated Scottish forces under William Wallace, whose schiltron formations were broken by English archers, ending Wallace's leadership of the Scottish resistance.

entries.name: Battle of Berestechko
entries.desc: In 1651, the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth defeated a Cossack and Crimean Tatar army near Berestechko, the largest battle of the Khmelnytsky Uprising. The Tatars' withdrawal forced harsher peace terms on the Cossacks.

entries.name: Treaty of Alcáçovas
entries.desc: The Treaty of Alcáçovas was signed on 4 September 1479 between the Catholic Monarchs of Castile and Aragon on one side and Afonso V and his son, Prince John of Portugal, on the other side. It put a…

entries.name: Battle of Badon
entries.desc: A battle traditionally dated to around 500 CE in which Britons are said to have defeated invading Anglo-Saxons. Its historicity is disputed; it is chiefly known through its later link to the legend of King Arthur.

entries.name: Battle of the Vorskla River
entries.desc: On 12 August 1399, Golden Horde forces under Edigu crushed a Lithuanian-led coalition at the Vorskla River, halting Grand Duke Vytautas's eastward expansion and securing Tatar dominance over the steppe for years.

entries.name: Battle of Tricamarum
entries.desc: On 15 December 533, Byzantine general Belisarius decisively defeated the Vandal army, effectively ending the Vandal Kingdom and returning North Africa to Roman rule.

entries.name: Battle of Durbe
entries.desc: On 13 July 1260, Samogitian forces defeated the Livonian Order near Durbe in present-day Latvia. The defeat triggered major uprisings against crusader rule in both Prussia and Livonia.

entries.name: Battle of the Dukla Pass
entries.desc: Fought from September to October 1944, Soviet and Czechoslovak forces attacked German defenses at the Dukla Pass in the Carpathians, a costly offensive meant to support the Slovak National Uprising.

entries.name: Falaise Pocket
entries.desc: The Falaise pocket or battle of the Falaise pocket was the decisive engagement of the Battle of Normandy in the Second World War. Allied forces formed a pocket around Falaise, Calvados, in which Ge…

entries.name: Battle of Anchialus
entries.desc: In 708, Bulgarian Khan Tervel routed a Byzantine army led by Emperor Justinian II near Anchialus, forcing the emperor to retreat. The defeat confirmed Bulgaria's standing as a power on the Byzantine frontier.

entries.name: Battle of Nahāvand
entries.desc: In 642, Rashidun Muslim forces under an-Nu'man ibn Muqarrin decisively defeated the Sasanian army; the defeat broke organized Persian resistance and opened the Sasanian Empire to Muslim conquest.

entries.name: Convention of Peking
entries.desc: Signed in 1860 to end the Second Opium War, this set of treaties between Qing China and Britain, France, and Russia ceded Kowloon to Britain, opened new treaty ports, and legalized the opium trade in China.

entries.name: Siege of Szigetvár
entries.desc: The siege of Szigetvár or the Battle of Szigeth was an Ottoman siege of the fortress of Szigetvár in the Kingdom of Hungary. The fort had blocked Sultan Suleiman's line of advance towards Vienna in…

entries.name: Battle of Peleliu
entries.desc: Fought from September to November 1944 for an airfield on the island of Peleliu, this battle produced some of the highest casualty rates of the Pacific War and remains debated for its limited strategic value.

entries.name: Battle of Civitate
entries.desc: On 18 June 1053, Norman forces in southern Italy defeated a coalition army assembled by Pope Leo IX and captured the pope. The victory secured Norman rule and led the papacy to instead ally with the Normans.

entries.name: Castellammarese War
entries.desc: Fought from 1930 to 1931 between rival Mafia factions led by Joe Masseria and Salvatore Maranzano, this power struggle ended with both men's deaths and reorganization of the American Mafia into the Five Families system.

entries.name: Treaty of Tientsin
entries.desc: The Treaty of Tientsin, also known as the Treaty of Tianjin, is a collective name for several unequal treaties signed at Tianjin in June 1858. The Qing dynasty, Russian Empire, Second French Empire…

entries.name: First Battle of the Isonzo
entries.desc: The First Battle of the Isonzo was fought between the armies of Italy and Austria-Hungary on the northeastern Italian Front in World War I, between 23 June and 7 July 1915.

entries.name: Anglo-Egyptian War
entries.desc: The British conquest of Egypt, also known as the 2nd Anglo-Egyptian War, occurred in 1882 between mostly Egyptian and Sudanese forces under Ahmed 'Urabi and the United Kingdom.

entries.name: First Anglo-Mysore War
entries.desc: The First Anglo-Mysore War (1767–1769) was a conflict in India between the Sultanate of Mysore and the East India Company. The war was instigated in part by the machinations of Asaf Jah II, the Niz…

entries.name: Third Anglo-Maratha War
entries.desc: The Third Anglo-Maratha War (1817–1819) was the final and decisive conflict between Britain and the Maratha Empire. The war left the Company in control of most of India.

entries.name: Anglo-Egyptian treaty of 1936
entries.desc: This treaty between Britain and Egypt ended Britain's military occupation of most of Egypt but let British troops remain to defend the Suez Canal Zone, and paved the way for Egypt to join the League of Nations.

entries.name: Anglo-Persian War
entries.desc: Fought in 1856–1857 after Persia besieged Herat in violation of an earlier pledge to Britain, this war ended with the Treaty of Paris, under which Persia withdrew its claim to Herat and Afghanistan.

entries.name: Fourth Anglo-Mysore War
entries.desc: The Fourth Anglo-Mysore War was a conflict in South India during which the Mysore State fought against the East India Company, Maratha Empire and the Hyderabad State in 1798–99.

entries.name: Battle of Mortimer's Cross
entries.desc: The Battle of Mortimer's Cross was fought on 2 February, 1461 near Kingsland, Herefordshire, not far from the Welsh border. It was a major battle of the Wars of the Roses.

entries.name: Battle of Ager Sanguinis
entries.desc: On 28 June 1119, an Artuqid army under Ilghazi annihilated the Crusader field army of Antioch near Sarmada, killing its ruler Roger of Salerno. Antioch survived only because the Turks failed to press their advantage.

entries.name: Aragonese Crusade
entries.desc: A 1284–1285 papal-sanctioned invasion of the Crown of Aragon by France, launched to punish King Peter III for seizing Sicily from the Angevins. The campaign collapsed after disease and defeat forced a French retreat.

entries.name: Battle of Karbala
entries.desc: On 10 October 680, Umayyad forces killed Husayn ibn Ali, grandson of the Prophet Muhammad, and his companions near the Euphrates, a trauma that deepened the Sunni–Shia split and is commemorated annually as Ashura.

entries.name: Battle of Taierzhuang
entries.desc: The Battle of Taierzhuang took place during the Second Sino-Japanese War in 1938. It was fought between the armies of the Republic of China and the Empire of Japan at the peak of the Xuzhou Campaign.

entries.name: Battle of Lutter
entries.desc: On 27 August 1626, Catholic League forces under Tilly defeated Christian IV of Denmark during the Thirty Years' War, forcing Denmark's withdrawal and exposing northern Germany to imperial control.

entries.name: Byzantine–Ottoman wars
entries.desc: A prolonged series of conflicts from the late 13th century onward between the shrinking Byzantine Empire and the rising Ottoman Turks, ending with the fall of Constantinople in 1453 and the empire's extinction.

entries.name: Battle of Idistaviso
entries.desc: In 16 CE, Roman legions under Germanicus defeated Germanic tribes led by Arminius near the Weser River. Despite the victory, Rome abandoned further campaigns beyond the Rhine soon after.

entries.name: Deluge
entries.desc: A deluge is a large downpour of rain, often a flood.

entries.name: Kalmar War
entries.desc: The Kalmar War (1611–1613) was fought between Denmark–Norway and Sweden. Though Denmark–Norway soon gained the upper hand, it was unable to defeat Sweden entirely.

entries.name: First Russo-Turkish War
entries.desc: The Russo-Turkish War (1568–1570) or Don-Volga-Astrakhan campaign of 1569 was a war between the Tsardom of Russia and the Ottoman Empire over the Astrakhan Khanate. It was the first of twelve Russo…

entries.name: Russo-Polish War
entries.desc: This is a list of armed conflicts between Poland and Russia.

entries.name: Battle of Towton
entries.desc: The Battle of Towton took place on 29 March 1461 during the Wars of the Roses, near Towton in North Yorkshire. Yorkist forces decisively defeated Lancastrian supporters of Henry VI, securing the English throne for Edward IV.

entries.name: Battle of Pavia
entries.desc: The Battle of Pavia, fought on the morning of 24 February 1525, was the decisive engagement of the Italian War of 1521–1526 between the Kingdom of France and the Habsburg Empire of Charles V.

entries.name: War of the League of Cambrai
entries.desc: The War of the League of Cambrai, fought from December 1508 to December 1516, pitted France, the Holy Roman Empire, the Papal States, and Venice against each other as part of the wider Italian Wars.

entries.name: Battle of Marj Ayyun
entries.desc: The Battle of Marj Ayyun was fought near the Litani River in June 1179 between the Kingdom of Jerusalem under Baldwin IV and the Ayyubid armies of Saladin, ending in a decisive Muslim victory.

entries.name: Fifth Russo-Turkish War
entries.desc: The Russo-Turkish War of 1735–1739 pitted Russia against the Ottoman Empire over the Crimean Tatars and access to the Black Sea, joined in 1737 by the Habsburg monarchy on Russia's side.

entries.name: Smyrniote crusades
entries.desc: The Smyrniote crusades (1343–1351) were two Crusades sent by Pope Clement VI against the Beylik of Aydin under Umur Bey, targeting the coastal city of Smyrna in Asia Minor.

entries.name: Battle of Tolvajärvi
entries.desc: The Battle of Tolvajärvi began on 12 December 1939 and lasted about a week and a half between Finland and the Soviet Union, marking the first large Finnish offensive victory of the Winter War.

entries.name: Battle of Kruty
entries.desc: The Battle of Kruty took place on January 29 or 30, 1918, near Kruty railway station northeast of Kyiv, Ukraine, during the Ukrainian War of Independence.

entries.name: Battle of the Boyne
entries.desc: The Battle of the Boyne, fought in 1690 across the River Boyne near Drogheda in Ireland, pitted the deposed King James II against King William III, ending in William's victory.

entries.name: Battle of Dublin
entries.desc: The Battle of Dublin was a week of street battles in Dublin from 28 June to 5 July 1922, marking the beginning of the Irish Civil War between the Provisional Government and anti-Treaty IRA forces.

entries.name: Franco-Dutch War
entries.desc: The Franco-Dutch War, 1672 to 1678, was fought primarily between France and the Dutch Republic, with both sides backed at different times by a variety of allies.

entries.name: Battle of Patay
entries.desc: The Battle of Patay, fought on 18 June 1429 during the Hundred Years' War, was the culmination of the Loire Campaign, where French forces inflicted heavy casualties on the English army.

entries.name: Treaty of 1818
entries.desc: The Treaty of 1818, an international treaty signed between the United States and the United Kingdom, resolved standing boundary and fisheries disputes and allowed joint occupation of Oregon Country.

entries.name: Battle of Culloden
entries.desc: The Battle of Culloden took place on 16 April 1746 near Inverness in the Scottish Highlands, where a Jacobite army under Charles Edward Stuart was decisively defeated, ending the 1745 rising.

entries.name: Indo-Pakistani War of 1947–1948
entries.desc: The India–Pakistan war of 1947–1948 was fought between India and Pakistan over the princely state of Jammu and Kashmir, the first of several wars between the two newly independent nations.

entries.name: Battle of Toulouse
entries.desc: The Battle of Toulouse (721) was fought between the Duchy of Aquitaine and the Umayyad Caliphate near Toulouse, France, resulting in an Aquitanian victory that halted the Umayyad advance.

entries.name: French Revolution
entries.desc: The French Revolution was a period of political and societal change in France beginning with the Estates General of 1789 and ending with the Coup of 18 Brumaire in 1799, reshaping modern political thought.

entries.name: Battle of the Caucasus
entries.desc: The Battle of the Caucasus was a series of Axis and Soviet operations in the Caucasus during the Eastern Front of World War II, following the German capture of Rostov-on-Don in July 1942.

entries.name: Battle of Lugdunum
entries.desc: The Battle of Lugdunum, fought on 19 February 197 at Lugdunum (Lyon), pitted Roman emperor Septimius Severus against usurper Clodius Albinus, establishing Severus as sole emperor.

entries.name: Battle of Trenton
entries.desc: The Battle of Trenton was a pivotal American Revolutionary War battle on 26 December 1776 in Trenton, New Jersey, where Washington's Continental Army defeated Hessian forces after crossing the Delaware.

entries.name: Storming of the Bastille
entries.desc: Parisian revolutionaries stormed the Bastille fortress-prison on 14 July 1789, a flashpoint that ignited the French Revolution.

entries.name: Second Northern War
entries.desc: Sweden invaded and nearly conquered the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, drawing in Russia, Brandenburg-Prussia, and Denmark–Norway.

entries.name: Battle of Cambrai
entries.desc: A British WWI offensive near Cambrai, France, featured the first large-scale, successful use of tanks in combined-arms warfare.

entries.name: Quasi-War
entries.desc: An undeclared naval conflict between the United States and Revolutionary France, fought mainly in Caribbean and Atlantic coastal waters.

entries.name: Battle of the Iron Bridge
entries.desc: Rashidun Muslim forces defeated the Byzantine army near a fortified bridge over the Orontes River, securing the conquest of Syria.

entries.name: Greco-Turkish War of 1897
entries.desc: Greece and the Ottoman Empire fought over Crete; despite an Ottoman battlefield win, an autonomous Cretan state emerged from the settlement.

entries.name: Second Barons' War
entries.desc: English barons led by Simon de Montfort rebelled against King Henry III to force him to rule through a council of nobles.

entries.name: Battle of Achelous
entries.desc: Bulgarian forces under Tsar Simeon I crushed a Byzantine army near the Achelous river, a major Bulgarian victory over Byzantium.

entries.name: Battle of Galicia
entries.desc: Russian forces routed the Austro-Hungarian army in Galicia during the opening weeks of World War I, capturing Lemberg.

entries.name: Second Russo-Turkish War
entries.desc: Russia and the Ottoman Empire fought over control of right-bank Ukraine amid Turkish expansion in the late 17th century.

entries.name: First Battle of the Masurian Lakes
entries.desc: German forces drove Russian troops out of East Prussia days after the German victory at Tannenberg.

entries.name: Battle of Mühlberg
entries.desc: Holy Roman Emperor Charles V decisively defeated the Protestant Schmalkaldic League near Mühlberg, Saxony.

entries.name: Battle of the Piave River
entries.desc: The Italian Army decisively defeated Austria-Hungary along the Piave River, a turning point on the Italian Front in World War I.

entries.name: Battle of Vittorio Veneto
entries.desc: A decisive Italian offensive shattered the Austro-Hungarian army, effectively ending fighting on the Italian Front.

entries.name: Battle of Zorndorf
entries.desc: Prussian forces under Frederick the Great fought Russian troops to a bloody, inconclusive standstill during the Seven Years' War.

entries.name: Battle of Mollwitz
entries.desc: Frederick the Great's Prussian army won its first battle, against Austria, in the opening clash of the First Silesian War.

entries.name: Mexican-American War
entries.desc: The United States invaded Mexico following the annexation of Texas, resulting in major territorial expansion of the US Southwest.
